name: Portugal
headline_status: Cannabis is not legal in Portugal, but possessing a personal-use amount has been decriminalised since 2001, and medical cannabis is sold in pharmacies.
summary: Portugal decriminalised possession of all drugs for personal use in 2001, treating amounts up to a 10-day supply (25 g of herbal cannabis or 5 g of hashish) as an administrative matter handled by dissuasion commissions. A 2023 law change stopped treating larger amounts as automatic proof of trafficking. Selling cannabis remains a crime. Medical cannabis was legalised in July 2018 and is dispensed through pharmacies.

possession_limit.value: Up to a 10-day supply, defined as 25 g of herbal cannabis or 5 g of hashish, is decriminalised; a first offence typically carries no penalty.

penalties.value: People found with personal amounts may be sent to a Dissuasion Commission, which can refer them to treatment or impose minor administrative sanctions; selling or distributing is a crime carrying possible prison time.

public_use.value: Using cannabis in public remains illegal and can be fined.

retail_sales.value: No legal framework for recreational sales; shops sell CBD and HHC products, not THC cannabis.

medical_since.value: July 2018, when legislation allowing medical use and pharmacy dispensing was signed.

home_grow.value: Personal cultivation, even for medical use, remains illegal.

tourists.value: The same decriminalisation rules apply to visitors as to residents: small amounts can lead to a Dissuasion Commission referral, public use can be fined, and there is no legal place to buy.

timeline.event: Possession of all drugs for personal use decriminalised
Medical cannabis legislation signed, allowing pharmacy dispensing
Parliament approves law ending the presumption that amounts above a 10-day supply mean trafficking

faq.a: No, but possessing up to 25 g of cannabis (a 10-day supply) is decriminalised and handled as an administrative matter rather than a crime.

faq.q: Can tourists smoke weed in Portugal?
faq.a: Visitors are treated like residents: small amounts are not a crime, but public use can be fined and there is no legal way to buy.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis legal in Portugal?
faq.a: Yes. Medical cannabis was legalised in 2018 and is dispensed by pharmacies with a prescription.
